historicalCases.lesson: When a provider frontend is alive but a fixed API is dead, inspect current provider-owned page/bundle metadata and rebuild route DATA instead of retrying stale endpoints.

Provider/Core logic must target the least-capable supported JS runtime; URL API mutations that work in Node may not work in QuickJS/native hosts.

historicalCases.lesson: Discovery may use hubs/upstream metadata, but released providers should execute against validated terminal/LKG DATA without GitHub runtime dependencies.

avoid: overwriting reliable hub with weaker discovery
historicalCases.lesson: Domain refresh must be monotonic: retain proven non-null LKG authority unless a stronger current proof replaces it.

avoid: treating route/stream count as native proof
historicalCases.lesson: Health/route evidence is weaker than native playback; classify per platform and lane before promotion.

avoid: mutating provider code solely to bypass CI challenge
historicalCases.lesson: WAF/environment failures are transport evidence, not automatically provider defects; compare profiles and keep them outside Repair mutation scope until provider-owned route behavior is implicated.

avoid: generic HTML scraping when proven API exists
historicalCases.lesson: A proof-owned typed API recipe should outrank generic scraping and be preserved as execution authority when route+recipe proof is strong.

avoid: disabling provider solely from one zero
historicalCases.lesson: A clean zero is not a broken provider; retain NO PROOF/candidate debt unless stronger regression evidence exists.

avoid: discarding manual A/B/C tests as anecdotal
historicalCases.lesson: Known-good manual cross-tests are durable regression fixtures and should seed provider/lane-specific LKG evidence.

avoid: treating one valid stream as validation of siblings
historicalCases.lesson: Playable-first must be fail-closed per stream: zero validated => []; otherwise return only streams individually validated.

avoid: assuming native blocking call is abortable
historicalCases.lesson: Use one Core-owned cooperative provider deadline and discard late results; native blocking bridges may remain unkillable and must be classified separately.

avoid: using historical filenames as current execution authority
historicalCases.lesson: Current structured DATA/runtime state is authority; historical artifact names are provenance only and must never drive quarantine or activation.

historicalCases.lesson: Activation is a current exact-bundle property: at least one supported lane must have playable identity-safe proof; route/type declarations alone are insufficient.

avoid: repairing provider when lifecycle is client-owned
historicalCases.lesson: If restart restores streams, classify stale request/generation/session state before provider mutation; lifecycle bugs can masquerade as provider regressions.

avoid: promoting current provider from historical proof alone
historicalCases.lesson: Historical success is valuable strategy memory, but current status/publishing requires replay on current exact bytes.

avoid: provider mutation for pure WAF evidence
historicalCases.lesson: For transport gaps, replay provider-owned current/LKG origins, request specs and domain memory before inventing extraction logic; peer experience is ordering evidence only.

Replay sanitized same-provider candidate programs first; historical candidate evidence is a high-priority prior but current bytes remain publication authority.
